original.description: Space Weather Centre for Spain Initial Establishment and Core Capability Developments: Part 1This activity will constitute the initial establishment and operation of a Space Weather Centre for affected stakeholders along with underpinning tools, capabilities and procedures required in order to deliver tailored high quality services to end users. Key user groups are expected to include operators of energy transmission systems, satellite operators, the aviation sector, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and others. The Centre shall operate in close cooperation with ESA's Space weather Service Network with the aim to establish a node that facilitates collaborative actions with network participants while moving progressively towards a structure with a clear operational dimension ableto support the development and delivery of tailored space weather capabilities and services. Particularly the centre will focus on translating complex space weather information from multiple sources into streamlined, actionable information. A colocation of the development and operations teams shall be foreseen with the aim to streamline the R2O process, support team building and to encouragedirect feedback to research, optimising the use of facilities in ESAC.Part 1 shall include: Systematic mapping of end users and establishment of key contact points with users and stakeholders Establishment of a proactive engagement strategy and actions with the identified end users to ensure full understanding of end user needs and operational requirements Development of necessary IT infrastructure, tools and service operation procedures in order to operate the space weather front desk, initially on an 8/5 basis, with on-call support during periods of elevated space weather activity. OoProcedures shall be developed with a view to transitioning into full 24/7 support at the start of a future Part 2 of this activity. Operation of the space weather front desk from KO+3 months for at least 6 months prior to the start of Part 2 handover Development of a space weather dashboard capabilities targeting end users and building on well demonstrated and tested space weather assets, constituting a layer for translating complex technical concepts into an easy-to-use tool for end users. Training for end users including exercises and simulations based on realistic use casesDevelopment of a roadmap for the operational Centre including priority R2O needs and the inclusion of a space weather testbed facility to be used for regional event simulations and training, bringing together stakeholders including end users, operators and domain experts with a focus on optimising the R2O2R pipeline. Support for data and product provision from existing assetsas part of the service provision shall be foreseen where it does not duplicate activities already funded via the Space Safety Programme's pre operational space weather service activities. Operationalisation of certain key models and tools along with their re-deployment within the Centre may be foreseen subject to the necessary licensing agreements with the asset owner. A handover to Part 2of the activity shall be foreseen.

original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test innovative III-V solar cell s processes and associated disruptive photovoltaic assembly technologies aiming to reduce the complexity, manufacturing and assembly time to meet the high demand of telecommunication satellites constellations. III-V solar cells will be developed and tested using thedeveloped processes along with flexible Photovoltaic Assembly (PVA) mini modules.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European source of III-IV solar cells and PVAs for satcom constellations by - At least a factor of 2 reduction of the epitaxial growth time- Enabling substrate reuse in the fabrication - Enabling a standardised and flexible PVA mini module for mass production of solar arrays.Description: In the space telecommunications sector, the shift from GEO satellites to LEO constellations requires advanced solar technologies that offer a balance of high performance, scalable manufacturing and proven reliability across diverse LEO mission profiles. Within this evolving landscape,III-V multi-junction cells remain the benchmark in terms of efficiency and performance, but complexity, manufacturing and assembly time must be significantly improved to meet the growing demand for constellations. In order to achieve this goal,innovative processes must be developed to increase the production capacity. Development efforts should not focus solely on solar cell technology but must also extend to the photovoltaics assembly (PVA) level, enabling the realisation of standardised modular and scalable PVA solutions tailored to constellation needs.This activity will focus on III-V solar cells and their associated PVA technologies. It will study and develop solutions to two main primary factors currently limiting the scalability of III-V solar cells:- Reducing epitaxial growth time at least by a factor of 2 by increasing the growth rate of III-V materials while maintaining high opto-electronic properties. For doing so, new and disruptive epitaxial growth processes must be developed.- Enabling substrate reuse in the fabrication through the implementation of innovative Epitaxial Lift-Off (ELO) processes either chemical or mechanical based. The ELO process provides a dual benefit, as it supports the production of flexible, ultra-thin solar cells (e.g. 30um thick) and contributes to reduce the use of critical materials in the substrate (e.g. Germanium recycling). A combination of a mechanical and chemical lift-off approaches will be studied and developed to optimise the overall ELO process.The resulting developed III-V based solar cells will be manufactured and tested. They will serve as a critical building block for the development of a flexible PVA blanket. Interconnection and encapsulation technologies will be developed and tested. original.description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. This BFIC will serve as a modular and scalable solution for user-terminal flat-panel arrays, enabling multi-band and multi-product compatibility.Targeted Improvements: - Frequency coverage extended from C-band to Q/V-band in a single BFIC.- Fostering high-volume production scalability and economies of scale.- Enhanced design modularity, enabling flat-panel antennas to scale in aperture size (same number of beams) and/or number of beams (same aperture).Description:Conventionally, different BFICs have been used in applications at different frequency bands, e.g., the C- to Q/V-bands relevant to satcom. Also, such conventional BFICs typically generate a single beam. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. Successful execution will position Europe as a leader in wideband BFICs, securing our competitiveness in the evolving satcom ecosystem. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.

original.description: The User Management Service contract will encompass a comprehensive suite of offeringsdesigned to support and enhance user interactions and experience for ESA and Third PartyEO Missions.This service contract aims at integrating the User Communication and Information Portaltogether with the User Management functions, covered in the past by separate contracts,whereby ensuring autonomy to Industry in designing and using communication tools asadditional instrument to reach and stimulate a dynamic and variegated user community.The Information Portal is expected to provide seamless access to relevant content and data,Graphical and Editorial Servicesshall deliver visually engaging and professionally curatedmaterials, and finally User Experience Benchmarking Services enable performancecomparisons and insights. A dedicated User Help Desk completes the suite assisting userswith inquiries and technical support, ensuring prompt and effective resolution of issues.User Management Services will implement personalized access to tools, resources, andaccount features through the management of authorisation and authentication services withprovision of a secured User Area. The User Management service will foster a user-centricapproach that prioritizes accessibility, support, and continuous improvement driven by userfeedback.The User Management Service contract shall include the following services: Operations, maintenance and evolutions of the web services for data discoveryaccess and retrieval of Earth Observation products and information (composed byEarth Online, eoPortal, Swarm Data Handbook, EarthCARE Data Handbook, 3DVisuals and Quality Reports Advanced Search platforms). Content Management and Creation, including editorial and graphical services. Operations, maintenance and evolutions of an identity access management infrastructure with federated identity access configurations. Support to user community via a unique and integrated user help desk which serves as the single point of contact for answering to user enquiries and complaints, facilitating data access requests, monitoring and ensuring user satisfaction, and providing communications about system unavailability. The user help desk function will also provide AI powered chatbots and virtual support assistants being powered by a comprehensive and well-maintained and updated knowledgebase. Management of data access requests, assign authorisation to users for accessing restrained data, in agreement to applicable terms and condition (including quota management). Management of a large set of user profiles, including asecure and personalised self managementarea to access and manage account information, access settings and transaction history tracking support requests. By centralizing these functions, the userarea enhances convenience, engagement, and control, allowing users to efficiently interact with the system and AI powered virtual assistant while ensuring their dataand preferences are protected.  User experience benchmarking services for systematic analysing and monitoring of user and stakeholder feedback (surveys and behaviour analytics) and monitor performance to help identifying strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement
